title: Reachability through a print simulation
statement: Let a counter program $P$ have a print instruction at state $l$, printing register $r$ and continuing at state $l'$. Let its simulated register values be $\rho$, and let $ps,o_0\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose every value $\rho(s)$ is at most $B$, $ps\le B$, and $o_0+\rho(r)\le p$ and $o_0+\rho(r)\le B$. Suppose the two oracles on inputs pairing $n$ ones with the binary expansion of $h$ answer, respectively, whether $h$ is less than the length of a fixed word $u$, and the bit of $u$ at position $h$, defaulting to false beyond its end. For every $d,j\in\mathbb{N}$ with $j+d=\rho(r)$, the compiled machine reaches the simulation state $l'$ from the print-processing state, on the input pairing $n$ ones with the binary expansion of $p$, starting with original registers $\rho$, pointer value $ps$, output-position value $o_0+j$, and temporary value $j$, and satisfying the prescribed state and register bounds at every earlier step.
